text: complete control, can write full GraphQL queries using meetupr_query(). useful wrapper functions don’t exist data need, ’re constructing complex queries multiple nested levels. GraphQL queries follow structured syntax. top level, define query operation name variables accepts. Variables prefixed $ must type annotations (like String! required string). ’s custom query fetching detailed group information: query demonstrates several GraphQL concepts: query GetGroupWithDetails: Names query operation (useful debugging) ($urlname: String!): Declares required string variable groupByUrlname(urlname: $urlname): Passes variable API field Nested fields like memberships { totalCount }: Fetch related data one request

title: Custom Meetup Queries
text: meetupr’s wrapper functions use template-based system combines reusable GraphQL query files R function logic. Understanding system helps deciding whether use wrapper function write custom query. Query templates live inst/graphql/ directory package. template .graphql file containing parameterized query. example, group_events.graphql might look like: << extra_graphql >> marker content extra_graphql parameter gets injected. call get_group_events("rladies-lagos", extra_graphql = "going"), meetupr: Loads template file inst/graphql/group_events.graphql Uses glue::glue_data() replace << extra_graphql >> "going" Interpolates variables like $urlname $first Executes resulting query Extracts data configured response path (e.g., data.groupByUrlname.pastEvents.edges) Flattens nested structures tibble
code: query GetGroupEvents($urlname: String!, $status: EventStatus, $first: Int, $after: String) {   groupByUrlname(urlname: $urlname) {     pastEvents(input: {first: $first, after: $after}) {       pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }       edges {         node {           id           title           dateTime           << extra_graphql >>         }       }     }   } }

title: Custom Meetup Queries
text: advanced use cases, can create meetupr_template objects define process responses: pattern used internally wrapper functions. process_data function determines raw GraphQL response gets transformed tibble structure users see. can customize handle complex nested structures perform computations extraction. details API exploration, see API Introspection vignette.
code: # Define a custom template with extraction logic template <- meetupr_template(   template = "my_custom_query.graphql",   edges_path = "data.group.customField.edges",   page_info_path = "data.group.customField.pageInfo",   process_data = function(data) {     # Custom processing for your specific data structure     dplyr::tibble(       id = purrr::map_chr(data, "node.id"),       name = purrr::map_chr(data, "node.name"),       custom_field = purrr::map_dbl(data, "node.customField")     )   } )  # Execute the template result <- execute(template, urlname = "rladies-lagos")

title: Setting up and Getting Started with meetupr
text: Meetup API limits many results can returned single request. max_results parameter controls pagination: meetupr automatically handles pagination behind scenes. makes multiple API requests needed combines results single tibble. Meetup API rate limit 500 requests per 60 seconds. meetupr automatically throttles requests stay limit. large batch operations, consider adding explicit delays:
code: # Get up to 50 events (may require multiple API calls) many_events <- get_group_events(   "rladies-san-francisco",   status = "past",   max_results = 50 )  cli::cli_alert_info("Retrieved {nrow(many_events)} events") #> ℹ Retrieved 50 events # Process multiple groups with delays groups <- c("rladies-nyc", "rladies-sf", "rladies-london")  events <- purrr::map_dfr(groups, \(x) {   result <- get_group_events(x, max_results = 20)   Sys.sleep(0.5)  # 500ms delay between requests   result })
